tax.text: Codiga supports abolishing federal income and property taxes and replacing them with consumption-based taxes and tariffs.
tax.quote: Property tax & the income tax should be abolished (not so fun fact, the 16th Amendment had to be passed to allow for an income tax - let’s repeal it!).

trade.text: Codiga supports tariffs as part of a consumption-based tax system while also saying trade generally creates wealth.
trade.quote: America should adopt simpler, consumption-based taxes and tariffs.

debt.text: Codiga proposes phasing out Social Security, government health care and other welfare programs as part of reducing government spending and dependency.
debt.quote: This means we must reform and phase out all welfare programs, including Social Security (the godfather of all Ponzi schemes), government healthcare, and government-backed mortgages.

housing.text: Codiga supports sharply limiting zoning restrictions to infrastructure and pollution concerns.
housing.quote: Zoning should be limited to genuine infrastructure or pollution concerns.

immigration.text: Codiga supports deporting violent offenders and people who exploit government programs, while allowing some assimilated immigrants a path to legal residency.
immigration.quote: A serious immigration policy should begin with deporting violent criminals and those who exploit government programs.

guns.text: Codiga opposes burdensome state requirements for carrying firearms and says gun ownership should be available to most people.
guns.quote: States should not create burdensome legal hurdles just to carry a firearm.

abortion.text: Codiga says legal protection for unborn life should apply in every state from conception.
abortion.quote: Since life begins at conception, the right to life is a fundamental right that should be protected under the law in every state.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Codiga strongly agreed that biological males should be excluded from women’s sports and sex-specific spaces.
gender.quote: Biological males should not be allowed to participate in women's sports or occupy biological women's spaces whether it be bathrooms, locker rooms, sorority houses, women's shelters, or prison.

health.text: Codiga supports market competition, price transparency and consumer choice instead of expanded government health-care programs.
health.quote: We must eliminate administrative bloat and expose healthcare to real market forces like price transparency and competition.

tax.text: Adams opposes cutting public benefits and services to finance tax breaks for the wealthy.
tax.quote: After 100 days under President Trump, his term can only be defined by economic hardship, divisive, partisan politics, and letting millions suffer for bigger tax breaks for billionaires

wages.text: Adams introduced legislation establishing a permanent minimum wage for federal contract workers that would rise to $25 per hour.
wages.quote: legislation establishing a permanent, predictable minimum wage for workers employed through federal contracts.

trade.text: Adams's office criticized President Trump's tariffs for increasing costs for ordinary Americans.
trade.quote: This legislation comes at a crucial time, as President Donald Trump’s tariffs and economic policies are driving up costs for everyday Americans.

debt.text: Adams said Social Security must not be undermined and described it as a lifeline for seniors and other beneficiaries.
debt.quote: Social Security is a lifeline for millions of Americans—seniors, widows, children, disabled workers—and we cannot and will not let it be undermined.

housing.text: Adams introduced a bill to expand affordable-housing construction by financing early development work on land owned by faith-based organizations.
housing.quote: a bill that would help expand the affordable housing supply by addressing a critical early-stage financing gap

schools.text: Adams opposes school vouchers and says public schools should receive the funding they need.
schools.quote: Adams opposes any school voucher program. She will always fight for public schools

safety.text: Adams's community-project funding page supported a civilian violence-prevention team for calls that may not require police.
safety.quote: The City of Charlotte recently created a violence and crime prevention team comprised of civilian responders.

immigration.text: Adams helped introduce legislation providing legal counsel and case-management protections to children and other vulnerable people in immigration proceedings.
immigration.quote: new legislation to protect children and other vulnerable groups in immigration proceedings by ensuring access to counsel, legal orientation programs, and case management services.

guns.text: Adams supports an assault-weapons ban, closing the gun-show loophole, and requiring firearm background checks.
guns.quote: ban certain high-powered assault weapons, close the gun show loophole, require background checks

abortion.text: Adams filed a brief seeking continued access to mifepristone and described abortion as health care.
abortion.quote: Women deserve healthcare, and abortion care is healthcare. This lower court decision cannot stand.

cannabis.text: Adams voted for the MORE Act, which would federally deschedule, legalize, and tax cannabis.
cannabis.quote: Voted FOR the MORE Act H.R.3617 in 2022, which provides for federal descheduling, legalization, and taxation of cannabis at the federal level

health.text: Adams introduced legislation expanding Medicare and Medicaid coverage for community-health-worker services.
health.quote: legislation that would improve Medicare coverage for community health worker services and encourage states to cover these services under their Medicaid programs.

energy.text: Adams introduced legislation using federal conservation funds to help farms transition to more climate-friendly production systems.
energy.quote: The IACA would use existing agricultural conservation funds to support farmers transitioning from concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) to more sustainable and humane production systems.

voting.text: Adams supports strengthened voting-rights protections and elections without unnecessary barriers to eligible voters.
voting.quote: Every eligible voter deserves an equal opportunity to participate in our elections, free from discrimination, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers.
